replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a statistical technique used to reduce the dimensionality of a dataset while preserving as much variance as possible. First, standardize the data to have a mean of zero and a standard deviation of one. Then, compute the covariance matrix to understand how the variables relate to each other. Next, calculate the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix. The eigenvectors represent the principal components, and the eigenvalues indicate their importance. Sort the eigenvectors by their corresponding eigenvalues in descending order and select the top k eigenvectors to form a feature subspace. Finally, transform the original data into the new subspace.
